newsitem.title: GERMANY: German official warns against tough EU farm reform.
newsitem.headline: German official warns against tough EU farm reform.

text.p: The European Union should not voluntarily speed up its farm reform efforts ahead of the 1999 World Trade Round, Franz-Josef Feiter, a state secretary in the German farm ministry said.
The 1992 farm reform package was a successful base from which to operate over the next few years, he said at a panel discussion organised by grain trade paper Ernaehrungsdienst.
"It would be wrong to give up positions ahead of new trade talks and to make conessions before it is necessary," he said.
"Experience shows that opens the door to new demands."
Feiter was alluding to anticipated demands from the U.S., a fierce competitor in world food markets, for the EU to further cut back farm export subsidies and price support.
He said the 1992 reform had successfully reduced surplus production and stabilised internal prices in grains and oilseeds although the beef market needed further help.

The reformed Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) could be easily extended to eastern European EU entrants, provided they were set long accession periods and given strict output limits for the time of full membership.
Feiter said he wanted an "organic development of the CAP, where the current elements were preserved."
This included proper protection on the import front and financial solidarity within the Single Market, he said.
